correctness.rationale: For centered Y=P(x-X1)/Delta the selected-pair contraction Aij=I-mu(ei-ej)(ei-ej)^T and centered pair noise yield exact conditional squared-norm drift E[S_{k+1}|Y]=[1-4mu(1-mu)/(N-1)]S+2(N-1)/N under constant utility, with unique stationary second moment (N-1)^2/[2Nmu(1-mu)]. The exact random-pair quadratic difference average is 2S/(N-1); the fast mean is (N-1)/[Nmu(1-mu)]. For nonlinear smooth log U, pair bias is tanh[(ell_j-ell_i)/2], and near-consensus localization by fourth moments makes rejected interactions negligible on k=O(Delta^-2). A centered-fast-observable telescoping/martingale estimate replaces pair squares by stationary moment; Gaussian selected-pair mean noise gives diffusion coefficient 1/N under accelerated time s=kDelta²/N. The drift is (N-1)ell_prime/[N(1-mu)], hence the integrable invariant Gibbs density has exponent (N-1)/(1-mu). Independent exact-rational contraction/mean-drift tests for N=2,3,5,10 and mu=1/4,1/2,3/4 corroborate coefficients, not the functional CLT. Hypotheses ensure Lipschitz drift and a unique diffusion; finite-horizon limitation is honored.

Gossip with stubborn agents and stochastic approximation does not dominate the same utility-driven fixed-N finite-horizon theorem.

value.rationale: Exact finite-population correction determines the invariant law of the limiting diffusion in a widely motivated stochastic interaction model and separates a rigorous weak-noise statement from a heuristic large-N closure. This changes quantitative prediction at small N (e.g., N=2), supplies a natural covariance identity, and proves concentration failure probability vanishes on finite horizons; importance does not rely on full stationary interchange.

scientific_limitations: Fixed N, 0<mu<1, initial Delta-near-consensus, independent Gaussian selected-pair noise, C3 positive utility with bounded log-derivatives, fixed confidence eps>0.
Only finite accelerated-time weak path limit and invariant law of limiting diffusion. No interchange with original finite-noise stationary regime or simultaneous N limit.
